text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nile waters to flow through the Sinai via the Peace Canal by next October. President Mubarak inaugurates the first stage of the canal which will initially irrigate 220,000 acres (89,000 hectares) and up to 620,000 acres (250,000 hectares) in the final stage. Mubarak says some residents of the Nile Valley will be moved to the new agricultural land after the digging of the canal.
- The United States vetoes the re-election of U.N. Secretary General Boutros-Ghali. An Egyptian statement regrets the veto and the secretary general insists on nominating himself again.
- Cabinet to issue important decrees today, including setting up a free zone to print and export Egyptian books and removing lead compounds from gasoline fuel without increasing its price.

- The isolation of Sinai is over. Mubarak inaugurates the third tunnel of the Peace Canal. Egyptians will have a new life instead of just crowding the Nile Valley. There is no going back on the peace process and (Israel's demand for) "hot pursuit" in the Palestinian territories will renew violence.
- Efforts continuing to combat floods in southern Egypt and the Red Sea provinces. Train tracks secured and traffic returned to Hurghada airport.
- Turkey buys white sand from Egypt to use for glass making.
- Egypt's external debt is $31 billion, minister says.

- President inaugurates third tunnel of Peace Canal. Mubarak says: "All our projects are national projects. The Peace Canal is the life blood of Sinai. The economic conference was 100 percent successful".
- Suzanne Mubarak gives the signal to start the Childhood Festivals.
- Cabinet to discuss today a new plan to face floods.
- State revamps management boards of 13 chemical companies. Members are young and members over 60 years of age to retire after a maximum of one year.
